newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West spot power rises with higher natgas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West spot power rises with higher natgas.

text.p: Wholesale spot electricity prices for the U.S. Mid-West rose Wednesday in tandem with higher short-term physical natural gas prices and amidst cold weather, industry sources said.
"With the jump in natural gas it gets more expensive to generate power," one markter said.
Spot gas prices were said to have jumped an average of 40 cents per million British thermal units on Wednesday.
Cold weather also continued in Minnesota and North Dakota while some units were down for repairs, constraining power supply, the sources said.
IES Utilities Inc's 538 megawatt Duane Arnold nuclear power plant in Palo, Iowa was likely to reach full output over the weekend after a scheduled refueling and maintenance outage.
The 440 megawatt Big Stone coal-fired power plant in Big Stone City, S.D., will likely return to full service on Sunday after scheduled maintenance, Northwestern Public Service said.

MidAmerican Energy Co's 515 megawatt Neal coal fired power unit 3 near Sioux City, Iowa, was likely to resume production Wednesday after being taken off line for a boiler tube leak, a company spokesman said.
Minnkota Power Coopertive said the 439 megawatt Milton Young coal-fired power unit 2 in Center, N.D., was likely to return to service Friday following boiler repairs.

In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak non-firm next day power deals were pegged higher in the $26.00-29.00 range from discussion at $25.50-27.50 per megawatt hour (MWh) on Tuesday, the brokers and marketers said.
Power from Canada was said to be scarce with Manitoba Hydro reducing exports in cold weather.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power prices were said to be higher in the $15.00-17.00 range from $11.50-12.50 on Tuesday.
Despite the jump in prices, trade in MAPP was said to be fairly thin, with those holding power unwilling to part with it.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) peak, non-firm power for Thursday delivery was pegged higher at $22.00-26.00 from $21.00-23.00 on Tuesday.
Some trades in northern MAIN were said to be done higher than the rest of the region near $29.00 per MWh.
MAIN off peak power was assessed higher at $12.00-14.00 from $11.00-13.00 per MWh on Tuesday.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Thursday delivery were assessed at $25.00-28.00 from $21.00-24.00 on Tuesday, the sources said.
Off-peak next-day ECAR power was notionally assessed steady at $15.00-17.00 per MWh.
December peak ECAR was talked higher at $21.75-22.75 from $21.00-21.50 on Tuesday, the brokers and marketers said.
January/February ECAR was pegged at $23.00-23.30 per MWh.
Peak non-firm power prices in the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) for Thursday were talked at $24.00-26.00 from $21.00-23.00 on Tuesday, the sources said.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP were notionally said to be steady in the $13.00-15.00 area, traders said.
December SPP was assessed higher at $27.75-28.75 from $23.75-24.25, the brokers and marketers said.
--Chris Reese, New York Power Desk +1 212 859 1627
